claim: Let \(h_n^{(r)}\) denote the hyperharmonic number of index \(n\ge1\) and order \(r\ge1\). Among nonsquarefree integers \(n>1\), the smallest index for which there exists a positive order \(r\) with \(h_n^{(r)}\in\mathbb Z\) is exactly \(n=45\). Explicitly, with \(M=45!\) and \(R=68700053771933018729983527085685223542008840099658203156\), every integer \(r=R+kM\), \(k\ge0\), satisfies \(h_{45}^{(r)}\in\mathbb Z\). This is a positive-density arithmetic progression of admissible orders, not an assertion of the exact density of all admissible orders.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity: An explicit arithmetic progression establishes existence and a positive density lower bound, not the exact density of all orders. The full text of Sertbas (2025) was inaccessible; possible unlocated equivalent treatment is a material novelty risk. The argument uses published nonintegrality at even and prime-power indices; independently audited status is not claimed.
title: The first nonsquarefree index admitting integer hyperharmonics
